definition: LEPOR (Length Penalty, Precision, n-gram Position difference Penalty and Recall) is an automatic language independent machine translation evaluation metric with tunable parameters and reinforced factors.
details: LEPOR (Length Penalty, Precision, n-gram Position difference Penalty and Recall) is an automatic language independent machine translation evaluation metric with tunable parameters and reinforced factors.

explainer.lead: LEPOR (Length Penalty, Precision, n-gram Position difference Penalty and Recall) is an automatic machine translation evaluation metric that is language independent, with tunable parameters and reinforced factors. It matters as an alternative to fixed MT evaluation measures.

tiers.eli5: It scores a translation by checking how many of the right word chunks appear, how closely their order matches, and how the lengths compare — like grading a translation on coverage, order and length balance.
tiers.practitioner: Its components (length penalty, precision, n-gram position difference penalty, recall) are combined with tunable parameters and reinforced factors, which must be set consistently across comparisons. A pitfall is that tuned parameters affect scores, so evaluations are only comparable under matching settings.
tiers.paperLevel: An automatic, language-independent machine translation evaluation metric combining Length Penalty, Precision, n-gram Position difference Penalty and Recall, with tunable parameters and reinforced factors.

explainer.example: When comparing two candidate translations of the same source sentence, LEPOR combines their n-gram precision and recall with a position-difference penalty and a length penalty to produce the final score.
